estimator.name: robust
estimator.label: Robust σ (IQR)
estimator.definition: R = E_est / p per event; σ/E = IQR(R) / (1.349 · median R) per momentum window, in percent, with type-7 quartiles: a σ-consistent width for Gaussian errors that a few badly reconstructed events cannot inflate.

interval.label: 95% percentile bootstrap of IQR(R) / (1.349 · median R) from N = 20, B = 2,000, each replicate's quartiles drawn exactly from its resample's order statistics (sequential conditional Betas), seeded [42, frame, shower, bin, 8] with frames and showers numbered as for the median.

weight.label: Fit weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ = SE / value the window's bootstrap relative SE (the SD, ddof = 1, of the replicates behind its interval), recomputed at the fitted value ŷ and iterated; the first fit takes the bootstrap SE itself. The Gaussian asymptotic law would understate these SEs.

calibration.label: The deposit is c·E_dep with c = Σ p / Σ E_dep per shower over the selection (c_sum), fitted once; it cancels in the robust and sample widths. c_median, 1 / median(E_dep / p) over the events with E_dep > 0, is the calibration the median rel. cross-reference (alt) takes.

estimator.relation: For unbiased Gaussian errors median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E, so a median relative error is quoted beside σ/E, never converted into it.

top.name: Energy (GeV) ⟶
top.rule: E = 1/x², an exact relabelling of the bottom axis; no data are plotted against it.

energy.rule: E = 1/x² of the 1/√E view's x = ⟨1/√p⟩: one exact bijection, so both views draw the same measurements.
notes: The E view's y range follows the windows alone, from zero: those with N ≥ 20 from 2 GeV, whiskers included; a window below 2 GeV never sets it. No fitted curve, band or extrapolation sets it: one that leaves the top is clipped there with a caret.
Fitted curves are drawn from 4 GeV, the lowest window edge any fit can use, to 80 GeV: solid over the windows each fit ran through, dashed beyond, where the curve extrapolates its form.

Each window is drawn at E = 1/x² with x = ⟨1/√p⟩, the abscissa the fits used, so a window on its fitted line in the 1/√E view sits on its fitted curve here; its ⟨p⟩, slightly larger (Jensen's inequality), is in its tooltip.

anchors.rule: Chosen on the whole table's bins, not the selection: the lowest bin from 5 GeV, the highest bin, and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres. A series whose anchor holds N < 20 takes its nearest window from 5 GeV in log E with N ≥ 20, named in substitutions; with fewer than two, no fit: the robust width has no weaker window to fall back on.

affine.note: σ/E = a/√E + b: weighted least squares over 2 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (1 refit). ν = 0: the fit passes through its points exactly, so there is no χ² test.

pinned.note: σ/E = a₀/√E, through the origin: weighted least squares over 2 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (2 refits). χ²/ν = 0.00372/1, p = 0.951.

quadrature.note: σ/E = √(a²/E + b²), fitted as (σ/E)² = A/E + B: weighted least squares over 2 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (1 refit). ν = 0: the fit passes through its points exactly, so there is no χ² test. A ≤ 0, so a = √A is undefined; A is reported with its standard error.

notes: The deposit E_dep is the producer's total_hit_energy and p its incoming_momentum, both read from the 59-column event aggregate: one shower per event, no hits.

Each window is the producer's integer momentum bin k, [k, k + 1) GeV, of the shower's own momentum. Per event R = E_est / p; the plotted value is the robust σ/E = IQR(R) / (1.349 · median R) in percent, with type-7 quartiles, its whisker the 95% percentile bootstrap of that ratio (B = 2,000, each replicate's quartiles drawn exactly from its resample's order statistics), and its abscissa x = ⟨1/√p⟩ over the window's events. It equals σ/E for Gaussian errors and is not inflated by a few badly reconstructed events; dividing by p event by event removes the window's own momentum spread and the estimator's bias, and c cancels in it, so the detector series does not depend on the calibration.
For unbiased Gaussian errors median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E, so a median relative error is quoted beside σ/E, never converted into it.
The detector series c·E_dep is a linear-sum benchmark, not a limit: a model that reads the shower's shape (leakage, compensation) can do better than a plain sum.
E on both axes is the incident momentum p as the producer writes it. For a massive species √(p² + m²) differs from p by at most m²/2p², 1.7% for a proton at 5 GeV/c.

Robust σ/E is reported, drawn with its whisker, fitted and allowed to set the y range from N = 20 alone, the robust floor: quartiles of fewer events interpolate between single events. A window enters the fits and sets the y range from p ≥ 4 GeV.

Fits: a/√E + b and a₀/√E through the origin, by weighted least squares with weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE (the SD of the replicates behind its interval, over its value), taken at the fitted value ŷ and iterated (half steps once the refits oscillate); the first fit takes the bootstrap SE itself. χ², ν = n − p and its p-value. Where χ²/ν > 1 the standard errors and the 95% band are scaled by S = √(χ²/ν) (PDG), and the band then takes Student's t₀.₉₇₅,ν rather than 1.96, since S is estimated from the fit's own ν. The band is the 95% confidence band of the line, not the spread of the events. The quadrature form √(a²/E + b²) is fitted as (σ/E)² = A/E + B and tabled, not drawn; its b and the affine b are different constant terms.

A fit whose residuals average more than 5 of the windows' own standard errors (ν ≥ 1 and S = √(χ²/ν) > 5) has a form that does not describe its windows: it is drawn faded, as a provisional fit is, and said so in its tooltip, the fit table and the drawer. The size of the misfit decides, not the χ² p-value: a window of hundreds of events has so small a standard error that the test rejects a form for misfits no reader could see.

Anchors: the lowest bin from 5 GeV (below it the sampling fraction is still rising), the highest bin and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres, chosen on the whole table so they do not move with the selection. A series whose anchor window holds N < 20 takes its nearest window from 5 GeV in log E with N ≥ 20 instead; with fewer than two such windows there is no fit, since the robust width has no weaker window to fall back on. The other mode fits every window with N ≥ 20 from 4 GeV, the 4–5 GeV window included, below the anchors' floor.
The top axis is an exact relabelling of the bottom one, E = 1/x²: a deterministic unit conversion, and no data are plotted against it.
13 of the 17 windows across the series hold N < 20 and report no robust σ/E (the robust floor); Sample σ/μ reports them from N = 2.
Shower: c = Σ p / Σ E_dep = 105.4 over N = 307 events, fitted once over the whole selection.
Shower: the median rel. cross-reference (alt) takes the median calibration c̃ = 1 / median(E_dep / p) = 62.37, over the 307 events with E_dep > 0.
The shower is named Electron e⁻: the species of the paired XGBoost models (electron).

The model series is the shipped XGBoost momentum regressor on the notebook's 20% validation split: 62 of the 307 selected events. The detector series uses every selected event, so the two series do not share their events.
Electron e⁻ · XGBoost momentum regressor · validation split: median response R̃ − 1 from no fitted window over the anchors' fitted windows, no fitted window over every fitted window.

A regressor trained on a bounded momentum range pulls its predictions toward mid-range, so its median response leaves 1 near the ends of that range: there it narrows a σ and adds a bias to the median rel.
Off the axis: 7 windows below 4 GeV (158 events across the series) have x > 0.5; they are listed in off_axis with their σ/E and not drawn.
